scenes.headline: The 92-Year-Old Janitor Worth $8 Million
scenes.stat_label: SECRET ESTATE LEFT BY RONALD READ (2014)
bullets: Fixed cars for 25 years and swept floors for 17 years
Even his own family had no idea he was a multimillionaire
scenes.narration: In 2014, a ninety-two-year-old janitor from Brattleboro, Vermont passed away and shocked his entire town with an eight-million-dollar fortune.

scenes.headline: Vermont Janitor vs Harvard Executive
scenes.right_body: 42 years of modest living + reinvested dividends -> $8M
scenes.narration: Ronald Read fixed cars at a gas station and swept department-store floors for forty-two years. Meanwhile, Harvard-educated executive Richard Fuscone retired early into an eighteen-thousand-square-foot mansion and declared bankruptcy after the two thousand eight crash.

scenes.headline: High IQ Fails When Ego Forces a Sale
scenes.stat_label: COMPOUNDING LEFT WHEN DEBT WIPES YOU OUT
bullets: Genius paired with lifestyle burn breaks in a downturn
Finance rewards calm endurance over credentials
scenes.narration: In Morgan Housel's The Psychology of Money, the contrast proves a brutal truth: finance is the one arena where calm behavior beats raw IQ buried under debt.

scenes.headline: Never Interrupt a 40-Year Horizon
scenes.stat_subtext: Small steady margins + decades of patience -> outlier wealth
scenes.narration: Read never earned a huge salary or used risky leverage. He simply saved small margins consistently and let uninterrupted compounding run for over four decades.

scenes.headline: Endurance Is the Ultimate Edge
scenes.stat_label: PROTECT A SURVIVAL MARGIN YOU NEVER SELL
bullets: Keep fixed bills low so downturns never force panic
Let decades do the heavy lifting ego cannot
scenes.narration: Protect a survival margin you never have to sell, because ordinary patience beats reckless brilliance every single time - which is exactly how...
